title: 38 per hour annual salary: How to calculate your full-time pay with casual loading and super
description: Learn how to convert a 38 per hour annual salary from hourly rates, including casual loading and super. See the formula, tax estimates and fortnightly pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on a 38-hour week, a $38 per hour annual salary equals approximately $75,088 before tax and super, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee on a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super. For example, $38 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $75,088 per year.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate under most awards. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. If your base rate is $38 per hour, the casual rate becomes $47.50 per hour. Using the same 38-hour week, your annual salary as a casual would be $47.50 × 38 × 52 = $93,860 before tax and super. The loading is paid on top of the base rate, so never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. As of 2026–27, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $38 per hour annual salary of $75,088, the super contribution would be $9,010.56 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit paid into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to calculate your 38 per hour annual salary

If you earn $38 per hour and work a full-time week of 38 hours, your annual salary is straightforward to work out. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = gross annual salary**

For $38 per hour: $38 × 38 × 52 = **$75,088 per year** before tax and super.

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a useful starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your annual earning potential.

### Fortnightly pay

Most Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. Weekly pay at $38 per hour for 38 hours is $1,444. Your fortnightly gross is $2,888 before tax and super.

### Casual loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of your base hourly rate under most modern awards. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave such as annual leave and sick leave. For a $38 base rate, the casual rate becomes $47.50 per hour. Your annual salary as a casual would be:

$47.50 × 38 × 52 = **$93,860 per year** before tax and super.

Remember: the loading is applied on top of the base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading when using a calculator. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works in different awards.

### Superannuation paid on top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $38 per hour annual salary of $75,088, the super contribution is $9,010.56 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional amount paid into your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax and take-home pay

Your take-home pay depends on your total taxable income and the tax rates for 2026–27. The resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a $75,088 annual salary:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: 15% of $26,800 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $75,088: 30% of $30,088 = $9,026.40
- Total tax: $13,046.40
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,501.76
- Total deductions: $14,548.16
- **Take-home pay: $60,539.84 per year** ($1,164.23 per week, $2,328.46 per fortnight)

These are estimates. Your actual tax may vary if you have HELP debt, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a more detailed breakdown.

### National Minimum Wage and award rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. Most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that may set higher rates. Check your award on the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page or use the [pay guides](/blog) to find your correct rate.

### What this calculation does not include

This annual salary estimate is a simple conversion. It does not account for:

- Unpaid overtime or penalty rates
- Allowances or shift loadings
- Salary sacrifice arrangements
- The Medicare levy surcharge or HELP repayments
- The superannuation guarantee maximum contribution base cap

Always use the [reference tables](/data) for the most current figures, and consult a qualified professional for your specific situation.

### Summary

For a full-time worker on 38 hours per week, a $38 per hour annual salary is $75,088 before tax and super. With casual loading, it rises to $93,860. Super is paid on top at 12%. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to try different rates, and remember to check your award or agreement for the correct base rate.
